name: BEAM AGENT

intro.problem: Research in this area spans dozens of papers, textbooks, and an evolving record of notes and code, and general-purpose language models have none of that local context, so dense, accurate prompts have to be assembled by hand.
intro.value: A local agent that indexes this library could give grounded answers that cite their passages, synthesize ideas across sources, and turn a short local request into a dense prompt for a larger model.
intro.approach: We build an offline index over the papers and texts, wrap it in an agent loop that chooses its own tools (search the papers, search the record, open code), and add an optional escalation path to a hosted model, vetting retrieval with questions whose correct passages are known.
intro.goals: The first goal is a light build whose retrieval passes that vetting, followed by agent actions and cross-source synthesis once retrieval can be trusted.

questions: Can a local index retrieve the right passage reliably enough to be trusted?
Does local context make the prompts sent to a larger model measurably better?
Can the agent surface connections across papers that a reader would not see at first glance?

timeline.label: Idea: local, offline research agent over papers, texts and notes

BEAM PIPE locked: tool choice, multi-step loop, proposed actions

mk1 build: index a few papers and one textbook chapter
Vet retrieval against known-answer questions, then add the agent loop
